newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan bolivar ends flat ahead of TEM auction.
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan bolivar ends flat ahead of TEM auction.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed flat at 465.00/466.00 bolivars per dollar as traders waited on the sidelines for the results of Wednesday's auction of benchmark Central Bank TEM bills, brokers said.
"It's a very liquid market and investors could easily start buying dollars again (if interest rates fall) so pressuring the bolivar," said one trader.

Analysts concur that the Central Bank currently faces a monetary policy bind. Either it can bear down on inflation with higher interest rates and a stronger bolivar, they say, or it can prod domestic recovery with lower interest rates and a weaker bolivar.

Although Venezuelan officials have recently expressed concern over the strength of the bolivar, "given the likely difficulty of defeating inflation once demand recovers, we would argue for the first approach," said New York based IDEA in a recent market commentary.
Local foreign exchange brokers noted the Central Bank canceled an open offering of Treasury bills Tuesday. "That points to an interesting TEM auction tomorrow," said one.
